listen.script: Good morning, students. Because of the very hot weather, this afternoon's football match against Al-Noor School will not take place on the outdoor pitch as planned. Instead, it will be held in the sports hall, at the same time, half past three. If you want to watch, please remember to bring your student ID card, because only students from our school will be allowed in.
listen.q: What has changed about the football match?

listen.script: Omar: Faisal, have you finished the science project yet? Faisal: Not yet. I was going to do it last night, but my uncle and his family came to visit, so I didn't have time. I'll work on it after school today. Anyway, Mr Khalid said we can hand it in on Thursday instead of Wednesday. Omar: Really? That's good news. I still need to add the pictures.
listen.q: When do the boys have to hand in the project?

read.passage: Last winter, Nora's class decided to do something about the amount of plastic thrown away at their school in Riyadh. At first, many students weren't interested, and some thought the idea was a waste of time. Then Nora suggested a competition: each class would collect plastic bottles for a month, and the winning class would choose the place for the end-of-year trip. Suddenly, everyone wanted to take part. By the end of the month, the school had collected more than 4,000 bottles, which were taken to a recycling centre. The head teacher was so impressed that the project now runs every year. Nora says the most surprising thing was not the number of bottles, but how quickly people changed their minds once they had a reason to care.

qs.q: Why did students start supporting the project?
options: They learned how dangerous plastic is.
There was a prize they could win.
The head teacher told them they had to.
that the project continued every year

speak.prompt: Tell me about a time you learned something new outside school, for example a hobby, a sport or a skill. How did you learn it, what was difficult about it, and would you recommend it to a friend? Why or why not?
speak.expect: At B1+ the learner can give a reasonably fluent, connected narrative of a personal experience as a linear sequence of points. They can use past simple, past continuous and present perfect with reasonable accuracy, and link ideas with because, so, but, although, after that and in the end. They can describe feelings and difficulties, for example 'At first it was hard because…', and give a simple opinion with reasons and a recommendation, for example 'I'd recommend it because…'. Pauses for planning and some errors are acceptable when the topic becomes more abstract, but meaning stays clear. They can keep going for about 1 minute without much help, and paraphrase when they lack a word. They are not yet expected to use a wide range of complex structures or to develop detailed arguments the way a B2 speaker would.
